intro.text: Inogen, Inc. is a medical technology business that primarily focuses on respiratory health. We develop, manufacture, and market innovative respiratory health products, including portable oxygen concentrators, or POCs, used to deliver supplemental long-term oxygen therapy to patients suffering from chronic respiratory conditions and the Simeox ® product for airway clearance treatment. In addition, we have started distributing the Inogen Voxi ® 5 stationary oxygen concentrator as well as the Aurora ® continuous positive airway pressure, or CPAP, masks in the United States. Our proprietary Inogen One ® and Inogen Rove ® POC systems concentrate the air around the patient to offer a source of supplemental oxygen 24 hours a day, seven days a week with a battery and can be plugged into an outlet when at home, in a car, or in a public place with outlets available.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Of the $209.8 million of our 2025 revenue derived from the United States, approximately 45.1% represented sales to traditional home medical equipment providers, distributors (including our private label collaborator) and resellers; 29.5% represented direct-to-consumer sales; and 25.4% represented direct-to-consumer rentals.

Pursuant to the Collaboration Agreement, we have started distributing the Inogen Voxi 5 stationary oxygen concentrator as well as the Aurora CPAP masks in the United States, and Yuwell has commenced distributing certain POCs supplied by us in specified countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
We typically enter into master service agreements with our major vendors for these components that specify supply requirements, quality, and delivery terms.
We rely on third-party manufacturers to supply components of our products.
We have elected to source certain key components from single sources of supply where we deem it appropriate.

In some cases, maintaining a single source of supply can allow us to control production costs and inventory levels and to manage component quality, but also may lead to supply availability risks and means our ability to maintain production is dependent on these single source suppliers, which may put us at an increased risk of supply disruption.

In order to help mitigate against the risks related to a single source of supply, for certain components, we have initiated second-sourcing initiatives to qualify alternative suppliers and develop contingency plans for responding to disruptions.

In addition, providers may reduce or eliminate purchases from us due to our focus on maintaining a prescriber sales team and pursuing rentals directly, which could be in competition with our providers in the United States.

We rely on a combination of patent, trademark, trade secret, and other intellectual property laws, as well as confidentiality agreements and other contractual and operational measures, to protect our proprietary rights.
Our business success and our environmental stewardship both depend on the efficiency of our global distribution network.

In addition, providers may reduce or eliminate purchases from us due to our focus on maintaining a prescriber sales team and pursuing rentals directly, which could be in competition with other providers in the United States.
We depend on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of our sales revenue.
Our future success will significantly depend upon the timing and volume of business from our largest customers and the financial and operational success of these customers.
We obtain some components, subassemblies, and completed products included in our products from single source suppliers or from a limited group of manufacturers or suppliers.
We utilize single-source suppliers for some of the components and subassemblies we use in our oxygen concentrator systems and our Simeox product.

We, as well as our key suppliers, maintain product liability insurance, but this insurance is limited in amount and subject to significant deductibles.
